kurals.tr: Thunainalam Aakkam Tharuum Vinainalam / Ventiya Ellaan Tharum
kurals.m: The efficacy of support will yield (only) wealth; (but) the efficacy of action will yield all that is desired

kurals.tr: Endrum Oruvudhal Ventum Pukazhotu / Nandri Payavaa Vinai
kurals.m: Ministers should at all times avoid acts which, in addition to fame, yield no benefit (for the future)

kurals.tr: Oodhal Ventum Olimaazhkum Seyvinai / Aaadhum Ennu Mavar
kurals.m: Those who say, "we will become (better)" should avoid the performance of acts that would destroy (their fame)

kurals.tr: Itukkan Patinum Ilivandha Seyyaar / Natukkatra Kaatchi Yavar
kurals.m: Those who have infallible judgement though threatened with peril will not do acts which have brought disgrace (on former ministers)

kurals.tr: Etrendru Iranguva Seyyarka Seyvaanel / Matranna Seyyaamai Nandru
kurals.m: Let a minister never do acts of which he would have to grieve saying, "what is this I have done"; (but) should he do (them), it were good that he grieved not

kurals.tr: Eendraal Pasikaanpaan Aayinunj Cheyyarka / Saandror Pazhikkum Vinai
kurals.m: Though a minister may see his mother starve; let him do not act which the wise would (treat with contempt)

kurals.tr: Pazhimalaindhu Eydhiya Aakkaththin Saandror / Kazhinal Kurave Thalai
kurals.m: Far more excellent is the extreme poverty of the wise than wealth obtained by heaping up of sinful

kurals.tr: Katindha Katindhoraar Seydhaarkku Avaidhaam / Mutindhaalum Peezhai Tharum
kurals.m: The actions of those, who have not desisted from doing deeds forbidden (by the great), will, even if they succeed, cause them sorrow

kurals.tr: Azhak Konta Ellaam Azhappom / Izhappinum Pirpayakkum Narpaa Lavai
kurals.m: All that has been obtained with tears (to the victim) will depart with tears (to himself); but what has been by fair means; though with loss at first, will afterwards yield fruit

kurals.tr: Salaththaal Porulseydhe Maarththal Pasuman / Kalaththulneer Peydhireei Yatru
kurals.m: (For a minister) to protect (his king) with wealth obtained by foul means is like preserving a vessel of wet clay by filling it with water
